=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- workflow-templates/validation-harness/python-mongo-repo-checks/Dockerfile.app.j2:20-22 | severity=major | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The `requirements_file` slot is interpolated raw into shell, allowing quotes or shell metacharacters to break the command and potentially execute arbitrary commands during the Docker build.
  WHY: Jinja2 does not shell-escape values and Docker `RUN` invokes `/bin/sh -c`; severity differs across reviewers, so the highest severity is used.
- workflow-templates/validation-harness/python-mongo-repo-checks/Dockerfile.app.j2:12-16, 20-22 | severity=major | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Harness packages are installed before `COPY` while consumer requirements are installed afterward, allowing consumer-pinned versions of harness dependencies to overwrite the versions required by repo checks.
  WHY: The sibling `python-mongo-flask/Dockerfile.app.j2` installs consumer requirements first and harness packages last, but this template reverses that effective precedence, so incompatible consumer pins can break validation at runtime.
- workflow-templates/validation-harness/python-mongo-repo-checks/Dockerfile.app.j2:20-22 | severity=nit | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The requirements-file handling does not provide a clear diagnostic for unreadable files or pip failures.
  WHY: `[ -f "..." ]` checks existence but not readability, so inaccessible files produce an opaque pip error; this finding is reported as a consistency and diagnostics issue rather than a new regression.
- workflow-templates/validation-harness/python-mongo-repo-checks/Dockerfile.app.j2:20-22 | severity=nit | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The new consumer requirements installation introduces unconditional network access to PyPI or another configured package index whenever a requirements file exists.
  WHY: Air-gapped or restricted-network consumers can now fail image builds, and the PR description does not identify this network-egress implication.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

- requirement: The PR description frames the fix as mirroring `python-mongo-flask`, which already installed consumer requirements; "Mirror python-mongo-flask".
  expected_change_site: `workflow-templates/validation-harness/python-mongo-repo-checks/Dockerfile.app.j2` lines 12-22
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  EVIDENCE: The Flask template installs consumer requirements and harness packages in a single post-COPY RUN with harness packages last, while this template installs harness packages pre-COPY and consumer requirements post-COPY, contradicting the stated mirror intent.
- requirement: The sibling non-mongo `python-repo-checks` family should receive the same consumer-requirements installation parity implied by mirroring `python-mongo-flask`.
  expected_change_site: `workflow-templates/validation-harness/python-repo-checks/Dockerfile.app.j2` after line 12 (COPY)
  confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: `python-repo-checks/Dockerfile.app.j2` installs only harness tools (`pyyaml`, `jsonschema`, `jinja2`) and has no consumer requirements install or `requirements_file` slot, so custom tests importing third-party packages can hit the same `ModuleNotFoundError`.
